verdict_reasons: Agent used a genuinely algorithmic orbital model (parametric circular orbits) with ~30 hand-tuned constants, well within anti-cheat thresholds
Mean SSIM of 0.8692 accurately reflects rough structural similarity with significant per-satellite angular drift at later frames
pHash similarity of 0.5885 (mean hamming 13.17/32) correctly captures perceptual mismatch from imprecise orbital parameters
Duration penalty of 1.0 correctly reflects matching frame count
All anti-cheat gates passed legitimately — no data extraction, no file I/O, no encoded dumps
Final multiplicative score 0.1056 accurately reflects a correct approach with insufficient parameter tuning
outcome_detail: Agent produced a working algorithmic orbital animation (mean SSIM 0.8692) but angular velocity errors for several satellites caused drift over time, yielding gated SSIM of only 0.1795 and phash similarity of 0.5885, resulting in a low composite score of 0.1056.
strategy: Extract reference frames, detect circles by color, fit orbital parameters, render Revideo scene
agent_behavior: Extracted 60 reference frames at 4fps and 361 frames at 24fps using ffmpeg for analysis
Used PIL and scipy.ndimage to detect 11 circles by color and track positions across frames
Reverse-engineered orbital model: 1 central circle + 10 satellites with distinct radii, phases, and angular velocities
Built a compact Revideo scene (55 lines) using createSignal and linear tween for time-driven parametric orbits
Rendered twice total — initial render plus one omega correction pass — then stopped iterating
Compared reference vs output frames visually and numerically (angular error per satellite per frame)
Recognized angular drift for outer satellites at late frames but did not attempt further refinement
Completed all 3 self-assigned tasks within ~14 minutes of agent execution time
